description: Use this when the user wants to see or inspect one specific 00Widget card. It reads the current card by stable id and opens a read-only visual preview. Prefer this over render_dashboard when a single card answers the request.

id.description: The stable id of the card to preview.

name: render_card

confirm.description: Ask the person before running. Also stops the button running from a widget, for the same reason `role: destructive` does.

confirmation.description: Custom copy for the foreground confirmation alert. Older actions may omit it; clients then explain that 00Widget will send the named action for the card.

message.description: Plain-language consequence shown beneath the confirmation title.

title.description: Question shown as the confirmation title, such as "Approve launch?".

id.description: Stable id for the button. It is the `/v1/actions/<id>/run` path segment and is echoed back in the webhook delivery.

label.description: What the button says. Short enough for a widget: "Boost 1h", "Retry".

role.description: `destructive` marks the button as dangerous and stops it running from a widget; it routes through the iOS app for confirmation instead.

briefing.description: Ordered prose behind a `briefing` card. Keep `value` as the compact conclusion and `subtitle` as its first explanation: old clients render the unknown template as a summary and still show both.

sections.description: Progressive details, most important first. The card's value and subtitle are the compact conclusion and old-client fallback.

id.description: Stable id for this detail. Order sections from most important to least: smaller surfaces show only a prefix.

label.description: Optional short heading such as Cause, Impact, or Next.

text.description: One self-contained plain-text detail. Do not send Markdown. Make it useful without relying on a later section, because smaller widgets may stop here.

chart.description: The series behind a `chart` card. Republish the whole window every time — nothing is appended and no history is kept.

categories.description: Rich categories aligned with points. Use category signal for meanings that vary per bar, such as favorable off-peak and unfavorable peak periods. The server derives labels.

id.description: Stable category id for the time period or bucket.

label.description: Short display label. The server derives the legacy labels array from categories.

signal.description: Contextual interpretation of this category, such as a favorable off-peak or unfavorable peak period.

labels.description: Optional category labels aligned with points. Small surfaces omit them; large widgets and detail views show a readable subset.

max.description: Pins the top of the plot.

min.description: Pins the bottom of the plot. Without a range the plot scales to the series, so a flat-but-noisy one looks dramatic. Send at least `min: 0` whenever the absolute scale is the point.

points.description: 2-60 values, oldest first, plotted evenly spaced. There are no timestamps: send a fixed rolling window. The small surfaces — Lock Screen, small widget, grid cells — average a long series down to what they can draw, so the window you send is always the window shown; send the resolution the data actually has.

rangeValueLabel.description: Short meaning shared by every supplied ranges[].value marker, such as Daily average, Median, or Current. Omit it rather than guessing.

ranges.description: Two to sixty low/high intervals. The server derives legacy points from each value, or from its midpoint when value is absent.

high.description: Top of the observed or expected interval.

low.description: Bottom of the observed or expected interval.

value.description: Optional representative value marked inside the interval. Its meaning is supplied by the chart's rangeValueLabel; clients never infer one.

reference.description: A target, budget, SLO or threshold, drawn as a dashed rule across the plot. Usually the difference between a trend you can read and one you can act on, because above-or-below needs no axis labels. The rule has no numeric label; when its exact value matters, lead the card's short `subtitle` with its formatted meaning and value.

referenceMetadata.description: Optional label and semantic meaning for the numeric reference. Kept separate so older clients still receive and draw the legacy reference number.

label.description: Short name for the rule, such as Target, Baseline, Budget, or Capacity.

semantic.description: Meaning of the rule. Renderers choose its color, dash, emphasis, and accessibility wording.

flow.description: Whether a quantity flows into or out of the measured system.

role.description: What the series represents; affects emphasis and fill treatment, never a producer-selected color.

signal.description: Contextual interpretation from the producer's perspective, not an intrinsic property of the value.

semantic.description: Meaning shared by a single points or range series and inherited by any multi-series entry that omits a semantic dimension.

flow.description: Whether a quantity flows into or out of the measured system.

role.description: What the series represents; affects emphasis and fill treatment, never a producer-selected color.

signal.description: Contextual interpretation from the producer's perspective, not an intrinsic property of the value.

series.description: One to four semantic series for vertical bars, stacked or grouped when multiple. The server derives legacy points as their totals for older clients.

id.description: Stable series id, used to keep renderer-owned presentation consistent.

points.description: Non-negative values aligned one-for-one with every other series, label, and category.

semantic.description: Optional role, flow, and contextual signal hints. Renderers choose all actual colors and patterns.

flow.description: Whether a quantity flows into or out of the measured system.

role.description: What the series represents; affects emphasis and fill treatment, never a producer-selected color.

signal.description: Contextual interpretation from the producer's perspective, not an intrinsic property of the value.

stacking.description: How multiple bar series share each category: stacked into one column or grouped side by side.

style.description: `line` is a sparkline with a soft area fill; `bar` grows every bar from the bottom of the range; `delta` anchors at zero instead, so signed values grow up or down from a zero rule; `range` draws floating low/high intervals with optional publisher-defined value markers.

comparison.description: A concise interpretation beside the headline, for example +18 vs Monday. This is distinct from chart style `delta`, which controls bar geometry.

label.description: What the change is compared with, such as vs Monday or from last week.

signal.description: Whether this change is favorable, neutral, cautionary, or unfavorable in context.

deepLink.description: HTTPS URL opened when the card is tapped. Point it at the dashboard or detail page this card summarises.

icon.description: SF Symbol name for the card: sun.max, bolt.car, flame, washer, creditcard.

id.description: Stable identity of the thing being shown, reused on every publish so the card updates rather than duplicating. Never embed a timestamp or run id. Namespace it if another integration might pick the same name.

items.description: Rows. A `list` shows them as rows, ranked as bars when they carry an `amount`; a `history` draws their `status` as pips, oldest first; a `breakdown` splits one bar by their `amount`.

amount.description: The row's magnitude, used to draw it: ranked bars in a `list` (measured against the largest row) or proportional segments in a `breakdown` (measured against the total, so never send percentages). Send it alongside `value`, not instead of it — `value` is the label.

deepLink.description: HTTPS URL opened when this row is tapped, instead of the card's own `deepLink`. Only medium and large Home Screen widgets can address a single row; everywhere smaller the whole card is one tap target and the card's link is used.

id.description: Stable id for this row, unique within the card.

semantic.description: Optional role and flow hints for this quantity. Keep health/outcome meaning in `status`; items deliberately do not duplicate the chart/activity `signal` field.

flow.description: Whether this item flows into or out of the measured system.

role.description: What this item represents. Renderers choose the emphasis; producers never choose a color.

status.description: Colours the row. In a `history` card it is the entire content: each item is one past outcome and only its status is drawn.

subtitle.description: A second line under the row's title.

value.description: The row's reading, as a display string already formatted for a person.

priority.description: Where this card sits among the tenant's cards. Higher comes first; absent counts as 0 and ties break by `id`, which is the order everything had before. It decides the order of `GET /v1/cards`, the app's dashboard, and which cards fill a Home Screen grid widget that has not been configured with specific ones.

producer.description: Who published this card. Use the operator's own agent or automation name, not a provider logo; compact surfaces omit this attribution to preserve space.

icon.description: Optional SF Symbol shown beside the producer on roomy Apple surfaces.

label.description: Human-readable name of the agent, automation, or service that published the card.

progress.description: How full the thing is, 0-1, drawn as a bar. Required in practice by `template: progress`, ignored where there is nowhere to draw it. Keep `value` as the label, so the card can show both: "184 of 240".

status.description: Drives the card's tint and badge on every surface. `good`/`warning`/`critical` for health, `running`/`finished`/`paused`/`offline` for lifecycle.

statusIcon.description: A second SF Symbol for a runtime state that changes independently of what the card is — bolt.fill while boosting, arrow.up while charging. Drawn at every widget size, including grid cells.

subtitle.description: A short, single-line label under the title or value. It truncates rather than wraps on widgets, so aim for about 40 characters, put essential numbers and qualifiers first, and do not repeat the title. For a chart whose `reference` matters, lead with its formatted meaning and value: "$300 baseline · Mar–Aug 2026".

template.description: How the card is drawn. Pick by the shape of the data, not the domain: `summary` for one headline number or short state; `progress` for something filling up; `list` for 2-6 things with their own values; `action` for buttons; `chart` for one number moving over time; `history` for a run of pass/fail outcomes; `breakdown` for a whole split into parts; `briefing` for a conclusion followed by ordered prose; `timeline` for irregular timestamped events and duration spans. When unsure, `summary` degrades best at every widget size.

timeline.description: Timestamped events and spans behind a `timeline` card. Republish the complete fixed window; the server sorts entries and does not append history.

endAt.description: End of the fixed observation window.

entries.description: Events and spans in the window. The server stores them oldest first; republish the complete window.

at.description: When the event happened, or when a duration began.

endAt.description: When a duration ended. Omit for an instantaneous event.

id.description: Stable id for this event within the published window.

label.description: Optional entry-specific detail. The series label already names the event kind.

laneId.description: The lane on which this entry is drawn.

seriesId.description: The event series this entry belongs to.

status.description: Optional health or lifecycle meaning for this entry. Never use it merely to choose a colour.

lanes.description: One to three horizontal subjects, in display order.

id.description: Stable lane id, referenced by every timeline entry.

label.description: Short label for one observed subject, such as Whole house, Garage, or Production.

series.description: One to four event kinds, in stable legend order.

icon.description: Optional SF Symbol for the series. Renderers own its colour and marker treatment.

id.description: Stable event-series id, referenced by every timeline entry.

label.description: Short legend label for this kind of event or span.

startAt.description: Beginning of the fixed observation window.

title.description: The name of the thing. It renders on one line at caption size, so keep it short and stable — a value that moves belongs in `value`.

unit.description: Suffix shown after `value`: kW, %, jobs. Prefixes such as currency symbols belong in the formatted `value` instead; use `value: "$338.99"` and omit `unit`, not `value: "338.99"` with `unit: "$"`.

value.description: The headline, as a display string already formatted for a person: "3.2", "$338.99", "4m 12s", "Healthy". It is never parsed back into a number.
